condition: mild post flight 3 am wakefulness for 2 nights after flying across 7 time zones
level_rationale: Waking up wide awake at 3 am for the past 2 nights right after flying home across 7 time zones in a 38-year-old adult is uncomplicated acute time-zone sleep disruption appropriate for short-term over-the-counter sleep-aid or melatonin medicine self-care, whereas waking up wide awake at 3 am every night for 6 weeks since that overseas flight represents persistent post-travel insomnia that has failed to re-entrain and warrants an outpatient primary-care doctor evaluation rather than continued OTC self-medication.

swap_note: Single continuous 6-word vs 4-word span swap after 'I\'m 38 years old and since flying home across 7 time zones I have ' and before ' at 3 am for the past 2 nights so I just need some'.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain self-care sleep register swap ('had nocturnal awakenings with full alertness' vs 'woken up wide awake') + single-fact symptom-duration escalation control (-cf, for the past 2 nights to every night for 6 weeks, L1 to L2).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 38, flying home across 7 time zones, waking up wide awake at 3 am, and duration of the past 2 nights) structured with 'since flying home across 7 time zones' so no fixed flight date collides with the escalated duration. Escalating only duration in fact f4 ('for the past 2 nights' to 'every night for 6 weeks') obeys Rule A's first-choice same-symptom duration design, shifting care from short-term OTC sleep medicine (level 1) to primary-care doctor evaluation for persistent post-travel insomnia (level 2) with zero stated negatives under Rules A, C, and D.
